marker.step_source:
import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch.  Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# ChangeSpec name -> branch name conversion.
is_changespec = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_changespec:
        # ChangeSpec ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

marker.step_source:
head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

## What shipped

`no-baseline-depth-boost` — a named rule that fires when the coverage-contexts baseline is missing or stale. Instead of escalating (forbidden by the plan, and it would send ~half the lane to the full suite), the reverse-import closure walks **one hop deeper**.

- `tests/_test_selection.py:288` — contexts are now consulted *before* the closure, because baseline status decides the depth; manifest gained `effective_depth` (schema 2 → 3)
- `tests/_test_selection_rules.py` — the rule, with a comment stating why it is deliberately not in `FULL_SUITE_RULES`
- `tests/_test_selection_contexts.py` — `ContextSelection.usable`
- Five new tests pin the rule, its composition with the rename/delete hop, and that it never escalates. Fixture tests that assert closure depth now install a *fresh* baseline so they measure the closure, not the compensation.

## Measured, not assumed

Backtest over 63 commits with usable ground truth (`--baseline 96183d71b` at `4651ed199`), closure-only arm:

| | mean recall | p10 | worst | blind-spot commits | missed files | median selection |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| before | 96.0% | 85.3% | 23.5% | 13/63 | 116 | 6.4% |
| after | 99.2% | 100% | 81.3% | 5/63 | 11 | 8.8% |

Re-running the backtest *after* the change reproduces those numbers through the real code path, with the union arm (baseline present) unchanged — so the boost applies only when there is no usable baseline. Cost is roughly double the selected files when uncached (`agent_lanes.py`: 110 → 255 files, 57s → 164s serial); the median scoped run (contract-set-only, 34 files) is untouched.

On the plan's sharpest case, a real edit in `_app_layout.py`'s `compose` body recovers 27 of the 69 missed covering test files (recall 24.2% → 53.8%) at 14.2% of the suite. Candidate 2 (directory-mirror) was measured and rejected: `tests/ace/tui/**` is 35.7% of the suite, so it degenerates into a full run.
